title: IRR with an exactly zero first NPV answers 1/v - 1 from the stored v = 1/(1+guess), not the guess
statement: In DNA Calc's secant iteration for IRR the first point is v = 1/(1+guess), stored to binary64. When the NPV at that point is exactly zero, the answer is 1/v - 1 computed from the stored v, not the raw guess, so two guesses that store the same v give the same answer. This took IRR from 533 to 549 matched of 734 full-bank rows, 16 won and none lost. Two other details were measured against the same rows. A residual taken from the raw guess, proposed in the research answer, was refuted: it netted -3 on the bank and -10 on 200 fresh two-flow problems and missed its own target row. The 200-step iteration cap was kept because a cap of 20 lost 3 matched rows. 185 IRR bank rows were unmatched when the bead comment was written.
basis: Counts are quoted from the DnaCalc commit message and the bead comment (full bank, per-row trace). The three cited rows are build 20131 readings: five guesses within 4 units in the last place of 0.21 for the same cash flows (three shown) all answer 0.20999999999999996, not the guess; they show the answer follows the stored v and are not themselves a zero-NPV test.
inferred: That Excel returns the converted stored v at the zero exit is inferred from the 16 rows gained; no Excel code was read.
